title: Reconcile clusters/iad-devimprint/main.tf vs live ord-devimprint cluster
description:
clusters/iad-devimprint/main.tf (tracked in git) manages a spot_spotnodepool against cloudspace_name = "iad-devimprint". Per prior project memory ("Rackspace Terraform Integrations Retired", 2026-07-11 correction), the iad-devimprint cloudspace was being replaced by an ord-devimprint cloudspace (Chicago region, gp.vs1.medium-ord), registered manually with rs-manager ArgoCD. Live-checked during this review (2026-07-20): kubectl against kubectl-proxy-ord-devimprint shows a healthy 6-node ord-devimprint cluster (v1.33.0) — the replacement is live.

No local .tfstate file exists anywhere on ex44 or the lab checkout for clusters/iad-devimprint, so it's unclear whether: (a) the iad-devimprint cloudspace was ever destroyed via Terraform vs. left orphaned, (b) this submodule's config is now pure dead weight, or (c) it was applied from some other now-gone location.

Fix: verify whether the iad-devimprint cloudspace still exists (Rackspace Spot UI or spotctl). If gone, delete clusters/iad-devimprint/ and, if warranted, add clusters/ord-devimprint/main.tf tracking the live replacement (mirroring the existing module's shape: server_class default gp.vs1.medium-ord, node_count matching the live 6 nodes). If iad-devimprint still exists as a zombie cloudspace, flag it as cleanup (note: per root CLAUDE.md, only genuinely-orphaned objects that no GitOps controller owns are safe to delete directly — a leftover Rackspace Spot cloudspace with no ArgoCD/declarative-config registration would qualify, but confirm before deleting anything with a spend attached).

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md — this drift is cited there as evidence for why local, unsynced state is risky.

title: Expose estimated_hourly_cost output per nodepool (node_count * bid_price)
description:
Neither outputs.tf (root) nor clusters/iad-devimprint/main.tf currently surface the running cost of what they provision, even though every nodepool resource already has both var.node_count and var.bid_price in scope. Operators (and the existing spot.jedarden.com spot-pricing-dashboard project) currently have to re-derive per-cluster hourly spend by hand from tfvars.

Fix: add `output "estimated_hourly_cost" { value = var.node_count * var.bid_price }` (with a short description noting it's bid price, not necessarily clearing price) to outputs.tf and to clusters/iad-devimprint/main.tf (and any future clusters/<name>/main.tf). Small, low-risk, output-only change.

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md (grouped improvement pass, low priority relative to the state-backend work).

title: Move rs-manager.tfvars secrets into OpenBao instead of a local plaintext file
description:
rs-manager.tfvars (gitignored, correctly) is the only copy of the credentials needed to re-apply against rs-manager: rackspace_spot_token, tailscale_oauth_client_id/secret, github_token. It exists only on this ex44 checkout's disk with no backup — the same single-point-of-failure problem as the local .tfstate (see docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001), except for the *inputs* needed to reconstruct rather than the record of what was built.

This workspace already runs OpenBao (root CLAUDE.md "OpenBao topology" — active instance at traefik-rs-manager:8200) and already uses it for other cluster secrets. Fix: write a small wrapper script (e.g. scripts/tf-apply.sh) that fetches these values from OpenBao (e.g. secret/rackspace-spot-terraform/rs-manager) and exports them as TF_VAR_rackspace_spot_token etc. before invoking `terraform apply`, so the plaintext values never need to live in a tfvars file on disk at rest. Keep rs-manager.tfvars.example (structure only, no values) checked in for documentation.

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.

title: Remove dead tftask/ image + its GH Actions workflow (retired Galleybytes terraform-operator runner)
description:
tftask/ (Dockerfile + entrypoint/entrypoint.cpp + usersetup/) is the container runner for the Galleybytes terraform-operator. That in-cluster automation (tofu-controller on rs-manager + Galleybytes operator on ardenone-hub) was removed 2026-04-22 after leaking ~48 zombie spot_spotnodepool objects (see docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 Context, and prior project memory "Rackspace Terraform Integrations Retired"). Nothing in the current manual-apply workflow (bootstrap.tf, clusters/*/main.tf) consumes this image.

Despite being dead, .github/workflows/build-tftask.yml still triggers on every push to tftask/** and builds+pushes ghcr.io/jedarden/terraform-operator-tftask on GitHub Actions. This also runs against the workspace-wide policy that GitHub Actions are disabled across all repos in favor of Argo Workflows on iad-ci (root-level CLAUDE.md, "CI/CD — Argo Workflows" section) — this repo appears to have been missed when that policy rolled out.

Fix: delete tftask/ and .github/workflows/build-tftask.yml in one commit (with a clear message noting why — retired automation, dead CI). Confirm first that ghcr.io/jedarden/terraform-operator-tftask has no other consumers (grep declarative-config and any tofu-controller/Galleybytes leftovers for the image reference before deleting, just in case something still pulls the last-built tag).

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.

title: Verify checksums for helm/liqoctl binaries downloaded in bootstrap.tf install_tools
description:
bootstrap.tf's null_resource.install_tools local-exec downloads helm (get.helm.sh) and liqoctl (GitHub release tarball) via plain `wget` with no checksum or signature verification, then chmod +x's and runs them directly on every fresh cloudspace bootstrap. A compromised mirror/CDN response or a silent partial download would be executed unverified.

Fix: both projects publish checksums — helm publishes a `helm-v${version}-linux-amd64.tar.gz.sha256sum` file alongside the release; liqo's GitHub releases include a checksums.txt. Add a `sha256sum -c` (or manual `sha256sum` compare) step after each wget, failing the local-exec (set -e already present) if it doesn't match. Small, self-contained diff to bootstrap.tf's install_tools provisioner block.

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md (bootstrap hardening, not state-backend itself, but found during the same review pass).

title: Commit .terraform.lock.hcl for reproducible provider versions
description:
The root module's .terraform.lock.hcl (pins rackerlabs/spot 0.1.4, plus random/local/null providers) exists on disk but is untracked in git (verified via `git status` / `git log --all -- .terraform.lock.hcl` — no history, and it is not in .gitignore either, it was just never `git add`ed). It currently only exists on this one ex44 checkout.

Fix: `git add .terraform.lock.hcl && git commit`. This ensures anyone (or any NEEDLE worker) running `terraform init` from a fresh clone gets the same rackerlabs/spot provider version rather than silently resolving to whatever satisfies `>= 0.1.0` at that moment — the spot provider is young and has already shown breaking behavior (see comments in clusters/iad-devimprint/main.tf about the admission webhook and addressOverride bugs referenced in root CLAUDE.md).

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md (state/reproducibility hardening pass).

title: Add Argo Workflows CI: terraform fmt -check + terraform validate on push
description:
This repo has no CI validation of its own Terraform code — the only workflow left (.github/workflows/build-tftask.yml, itself dead per a separate bead) builds an unrelated container image. A malformed .tf file or a variable typo currently isn't caught until someone runs `terraform apply` by hand.

Fix: add a WorkflowTemplate (or reuse `container-build`-style pattern) in jedarden/declarative-config under k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ that, on push to jedarden/rackspace-spot-terraform, runs `terraform fmt -check -recursive` and `terraform validate` (against each of the root module and clusters/*/ submodules) inside the hashicorp/terraform image. Read-only checks only — explicitly do NOT run `terraform plan` or `apply` in CI; per docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 Context and the 2026-04-22 tofu-controller retirement, automated apply against Rackspace Spot state is the thing this workspace has already been burned by once. This bead is scoped to lint/validate only.

Related to ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.
